salons.name: Copacetic Beauty Lounge
salons.model: Tiered service menu with some conflicting display and description amounts
salons.focus: Separate the displayed price from older descriptive amounts
salons.detail: Some color entries show one price beside the service and a lower starting figure in the description. Ask which amount applies before comparing a complete appointment. Keep those inconsistencies visible rather than treating the lower figure as the current quote.
rows: No foils or cut; confirm amount

salons.name: Fringe Beauty Lounge
salons.model: Artist-level ranges and à la carte color
salons.focus: Add finishing and tone to the color estimate
salons.detail: The menu separates color from cutting and blow-drying. When asking for a bright finished look, confirm the color placement, toner and finish as one complete quote. For extensions, separate the row installation from the hair purchase.

salons.name: Harmony Salon
salons.model: Starting prices; selected work by consultation
salons.focus: Check the selected stylist and current menu
salons.detail: The published menu gives entry prices rather than a quote for every stylist. Ask whether your intended color appointment includes the tone and finish in your reference. Confirm the current amount directly, especially when following a menu from a separate salon landing page.

salons.name: Whitehouse Salon
salons.model: Multiple artist-level pricing grids
salons.focus: Resolve which artist-level grid applies
salons.detail: The service page contains two pricing grids with different level names and some different amounts. The examples here identify the first grid's Emerging Artist column. Do not treat that column as a quote for another level; ask the salon which current grid and artist apply.

salons.name: Lost Sheep Salon
salons.model: Blonding packages with and without a haircut
salons.focus: Compare the same package and artist tier
salons.detail: Lost Sheep separates blonding with a haircut from blonding without one. Use the version that fits your actual visit, then check the stylist tier. A different tier or haircut inclusion can explain a difference before you even compare the lightening plan.

salons.name: Geno Levi Salon
salons.model: Starting prices, selected add-ons and consultation services
salons.focus: Distinguish a full service from a per-piece charge
salons.detail: The menu includes both complete-service starting amounts and itemized color options. Ask for the full plan rather than multiplying one line item yourself. Confirm the selected stylist, any additional color steps and whether cutting or finishing is included.

salons.name: Sognatore Salon
salons.model: Starting prices with explicit cut or finish combinations
salons.focus: Choose the correct color-and-finish combination
salons.detail: Color with a haircut and color with a blow-dry are separate menu entries. Compare the combination you actually want. If your goal includes both a shade change and a shape change, ask whether the quoted combination covers the entire plan.

salons.name: Dean of Shadyside
salons.model: Menu ranges with toner and length-related additions
salons.focus: Include toner and any length-related work
salons.detail: Several color listings expressly exclude toner or identify additional charges. Ask for the final combination appropriate to your length and current color, then compare it with another salon's complete proposal. A base highlighting figure should not be mistaken for a finished quote.

salons.name: Izzazu
salons.model: Starting prices varying by stylist
salons.focus: Confirm the branch as well as the artist
salons.detail: A salon group menu is a useful starting point, but your reservation is with a particular artist at a particular branch. Ask for that appointment's total, including any toning and finish. Keep the location consistent when comparing recurring availability and travel.

salons.name: Celestial Hair Studio
salons.model: Booking amounts with an hourly color policy and stated inclusions
salons.focus: Read the color pricing policy beside the booking amount
salons.detail: The booking menu and its hourly color policy need to be read together. Confirm the total reserved work and how included finishing applies. Ask about extensions separately, since a color inclusion policy does not establish the full cost of added hair.

salons.name: Alchemy Dry Cut Lounge
salons.model: Individual dry-cut rates and consultation-based color
salons.focus: Use the individual stylist's dry-cut rate
salons.detail: The site includes general service starters alongside artist-specific dry-cut amounts. Ask for the rate of the person you will reserve rather than assuming the lowest general number applies. Clarify how preparation and finishing fit into that appointment.

salons.name: Philip Pelusi
salons.model: Published ranges; confirm the individual salon
salons.focus: Treat the group menu as a starting point
salons.detail: The official services page publishes ranges, but the location and designer still need to be confirmed. Ask whether those figures apply to your intended branch and present goal. Do not substitute a retail-product price from the shopping site for a salon-service estimate.

salons.name: Studio Raw Elite
salons.model: Selected numeric listings; major hair services need a quote
salons.focus: Do not use a small-service price as a color benchmark
salons.detail: The service overview has some numerical entries but does not establish a complete dollar menu for the haircut and color options discussed here. Ask for the actual hair-service quote. A waxing price says nothing about what a full color visit will cost.

salons.name: Salon 13
salons.model: Technique-based cuts; color excludes a haircut
salons.focus: Separate lightening, root work and toning
salons.detail: The menu distinguishes the lightening area from root color and toning. Explain which of those pieces your goal actually requires. Ask for the combined quote, and confirm whether a haircut or styled finish belongs in the reservation.

salons.name: Salon Blanca
salons.model: Selected starting price and linked service categories
salons.focus: Identify the hair service before asking for a total
salons.detail: The salon overview gives a starting amount for Brazilian Blowout but does not establish a complete dollar menu for every haircut and color option. Confirm the Seven Fields appointment and chosen provider. Avoid applying a treatment price to a different service category.

salons.name: Salon Vivace
salons.model: Broad category starters rather than itemized service quotes
salons.focus: Keep category pricing attached to its category
salons.detail: The homepage groups multiple services beneath starting figures. Those headings do not establish a specific quote for every item within the category. Request the exact treatment or color service you want and its full inclusions before comparing it elsewhere.

salons.name: La Pomponnée
salons.model: First-time color consultation and an individual quote
salons.focus: Begin with the first-time color consultation
salons.detail: The color page directs first-time guests to a consultation to establish timing and pricing. Build your comparison around the proposal from that conversation. An online consultation reservation should not be confused with booking the completed color service.

salons.name: Head Space Salon
salons.model: Booking and matching route; no dollar quote established from the reviewed page
salons.focus: Match the stylist before comparing the estimate
salons.detail: Head Space's booking page points visitors toward its matching process and publishes appointment policies. Use that route to identify the artist and obtain an actual quote. The absence of a price on the reviewed page does not mean the salon has no pricing elsewhere.

salons.name: Pageboy Salon
salons.model: Stylist-specific booking links; no dollar quote established from the reviewed page
salons.focus: Use the correct artist's booking route
salons.detail: Pageboy's team page links individual artist bookings. A studio-wide search result is not a substitute for the service and provider you intend to reserve. Confirm the appointment address and ask the artist for the complete cut or color estimate.

salons.name: Salon Lachella
salons.model: Services and booking link; no dollar quote established from the reviewed homepage
salons.focus: Split routine services from an event plan
salons.detail: The homepage lists hair and special-occasion categories and links booking. Ask for the actual artist and service quote. For an event, explain whether you need one styled appointment, a trial or several people; those are different reservations and budgets.
